blocks.text: Physics is the most fundamental branch of the physical sciences: it provides the basic principles and laws that help to understand the mysteries of other branches such as astronomy, chemistry, geology, biology and the health sciences, and its tools, techniques and products have transformed our dreams into realities. Physics is an experimental science, and the scientific method emphasises the need for accurate measurement of the various measurable physical quantities. This chapter stresses the concept of measuring techniques and recording skills.

The foundation of physics depends on physical quantities, in terms of which the laws of physics are expressed; therefore these quantities have to be measured accurately. They include mass, length, time, velocity, force, density, temperature, electric current and numerous others.

blocks.title: Base and derived quantities
blocks.text: Physical quantities are often divided into two categories. Base quantities are not defined in terms of other physical quantities: they are the independent quantities in terms of which the others can be defined, for example length, mass and time. Derived quantities depend on the base quantities, for example velocity, acceleration and force.

The measurement of a base quantity involves two steps: first, the choice of a standard, and second, the establishment of a procedure for comparing the quantity to be measured with the standard, so that a number and a unit are determined as the measure of that quantity. Measurements must be reliable and accurate so that they can be used easily and effectively.
